title: Non-surgical model of perineural invasion to assess neural drivers of cancer in mice
author: Zaninelli, Saraiva-Santos, et al.

steps.title: Cell culture and expansion
steps.instruction: Thaw, expand, and passage B16F10‑Fluc‑Neo/eGFP‑Puro melanoma cells to obtain two confluent T175 cultures ready for inoculum preparation.

substeps.instruction: Thaw ~2.8 × 10^6 cells in a T175 flask by adding 20 mL DMEM (L‑glutamine) with 10 % FBS and 1 % Pen‑Strep.
Incubate 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 48 h until 85‑90 % confluency.
Wash flask twice with sterile PBS.
Add 5 mL pre‑warmed Trypsin, incubate 5 min until cells detach.
Add 5 mL complete DMEM to inactivate trypsin.
Aspirate cell suspension into a 50 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge 5 min at 300 × g, 4 °C.
Resuspend pellet in 40 mL complete DMEM and split into two T175 flasks.
Incubate 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for another 48 h until 85‑90 % confluency.

steps.title: Prepare injection site
steps.instruction: Depilate and clean the right hindlimb/medial‑right dorsal region of each mouse to allow clear visualization for subcutaneous injection and bioluminescence imaging.

substeps.instruction: Anesthetize mouse with inhaled isoflurane 3 % in O₂.
Apply sterile ophthalmic ointment to both eyes.
Trim all hair around the right hindlimb and medial‑right dorsal area with a pet‑hair trimmer.
Apply depilatory cream using a cotton‑tipped applicator; let act 2–5 min.
Wash thoroughly with warm running water, avoiding face and ears; ensure all cream is removed.
Dry mouse with absorbent paper towels.
Place mouse on a heated surface (~37 °C) for recovery; keep only part of the cage on the heater so the animal can choose a comfortable temperature.
Confirm the mouse is dry and fully active before proceeding.

steps.title: Prepare cell inoculum
steps.instruction: Harvest, count, and adjust B16F10‑Fluc‑Neo/eGFP‑Puro cells to a final concentration of 2 × 10⁵ cells per 50 µL injection volume, keeping the suspension on ice and using it within 1 h.

substeps.instruction: Remove media from both T175 flasks with a disposable 25 mL serological pipet.
Add 10 mL 1× sterile PBS to each flask, gently swirl to rinse, then discard PBS. Repeat rinse once more.
Incubate cells with 5 mL pre‑warmed Trypsin‑EDTA for 5 min until detachment.
Add 5 mL complete DMEM to each flask to inactivate trypsin.
Aspirate cell suspensions from both flasks and pool into a 50 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge 5 min at 300 × g, 4 °C.
Discard supernatant and resuspend pellet in 5 mL 1× sterile PBS; keep tube on ice.
In a 1.7 mL microtube, mix 180 µL PBS with 20 µL of the cell suspension.
In a second 1.7 mL microtube, mix 20 µL 0.4 % (w/v) Trypan Blue with 20 µL of the same cell suspension.
Load 10 µL of the Trypan‑Blue mixture into each of the two counting chambers of an Improved Neubauer hemocytometer.
Count live (unstained) cells in the four primary quadrants of both chambers and calculate cells / mL using the provided formula.
Calculate the volume (Z) of the suspension needed to obtain 2 × 10⁵ cells (Z = (2 × 10⁵ × 10³)/Y, where Y is cells / mL).
If Z > 50 µL, concentrate cells by centrifuging 5 min at 300 × g, 4 °C, resuspend pellet in 1 mL PBS, and repeat counting and volume calculation.
Adjust the cell suspension to a final volume of 50 µL with sterile 1× PBS.
Keep the inoculum on ice; use within 1 hour of preparation.

steps.title: Subcutaneous injection of cells
steps.instruction: Inject 50 µL of the prepared melanoma cell suspension into the right popliteal fossa of each anesthetized mouse.

substeps.instruction: Anesthetize mouse with isoflurane 3 % in O₂ and maintain anesthesia throughout the procedure.
Transfer 50 µL of cell inoculum into the cap of a 1.7 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Load an insulin syringe with the inoculum, expelling any air bubbles.
Place mouse in ventral position and secure rear limbs with adhesive tape.
Disinfect injection site with a 70 % ethanol pad.
Hold syringe parallel to the bench; insert needle perpendicular to skin into the popliteal fossa, inserting 2 mm of the bevel‑up needle.
Inject the inoculum, wait 5 s, then gently withdraw the needle.
Transfer mouse to a heating pad set at 37 °C for recovery (only part of the cage on the heater).
Confirm the mouse is fully active before returning it to the animal facility.

steps.title: Bioluminescence tumor monitoring
steps.instruction: Perform in‑vivo imaging of luciferase‑expressing tumors at designated post‑injection days using IVIS.

substeps.instruction: Ten minutes before imaging, inject D‑luciferin intraperitoneally at 10 µL · g⁻¹ body weight of a 150 µg/mL solution (e.g., 200 µL for a 20 g mouse, delivering 150 mg/kg).
Anesthetize mouse with isoflurane 3 % in O₂ and place in the IVIS chamber.
Within 10 min of luciferin injection, acquire an image with the following settings: exposure 10 s, bin 8, FOV 12 cm, f/stop 1, open filter.
Return the mouse to its cage after imaging.
Quantify radiance using Living Image software version 4.3.1; report values as photons · s⁻¹.
Repeat imaging on days 5, 9, and 14 (or 7 and 14) post‑injection as recommended.

steps.title: Perfusion, dissection, and fixation
steps.instruction: Euthanize, perfuse, and collect tumor‑nerve complexes, then fix them for downstream analysis.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a 10 mL syringe with 30‑G needle, surgical scissors, and forceps.
Make 1× PBS containing 0.2 % heparin (10 mL per mouse) and store at 4 °C.
Load a second 10 mL syringe with 0.2 % heparin‑PBS and a third syringe with 4 % paraformaldehyde (PFA), both kept on ice.
Euthanize mouse by CO₂ inhalation, confirming death with toe‑pinch reflex.
Place mouse supine on a dissection board; disinfect thoracic area with 70 % ethanol.
Make a lateral incision below the sternum to expose diaphragm and liver.
Cut diaphragm, expose pleural cavity and heart, then incise the right atrium.
Insert the 30‑G needle into the left ventricle and perfuse with PBS until blood clears and liver lightens.
Switch to the PFA syringe and perfuse until tissues appear pale (inject at ~5–10 mL · min⁻¹).
Make a midline skin incision on the right hind limb to expose underlying muscle, tumor, and sciatic nerve.
Carefully dissect and isolate the tumor and sciatic nerve, avoiding stretch or damage.
Cut the nerve longitudinally and proximally as needed.
Weigh the tumor on a calibrated scale and measure length and width with calipers.
Calculate tumor volume using: volume = length × (width)² × 0.548.
Submerge the collected tumor‑nerve sample in 4 % PFA at 4 °C for 24 h.

steps.title: Cryoprotection and cryosectioning
steps.instruction: Cryoprotect, embed, freeze, and cut tumor‑nerve tissue for histological analysis.

substeps.instruction: Wash samples three times, 5 min each, in 1× PBS.
Incubate samples in 30 % sucrose solution at 4 °C for 2 days (use ≥10× tissue volume).
Transfer tissues to cryomolds filled with OCT; add extra OCT to fully immerse and orient the sciatic nerve toward the bottom.
Freeze molds by placing them in a 100 mL beaker containing liquid nitrogen and 5–8 mL isopentane.
Store frozen blocks at –80 °C or proceed immediately.
Cut transverse sections 40 µm thick on a cryostat set to –20 °C; mount sections on positively charged slides.
If not used immediately, store slides at –20 °C.
Allow slides to sit at room temperature for at least 30 min to let sections melt and adhere before downstream assays.

steps.title: Immunofluorescence staining
steps.instruction: Perform antibody staining (or skip) on cryosections and mount for imaging.

substeps.instruction: Place slides in a humid chamber at room temperature; draw a PAP pen circle around each tissue section.
Rinse slides twice with 1× PBS, 10 min per rinse, covering sections completely.
If staining is required, block with 5 % bovine serum albumin in 1× PBS for 1 h at room temperature.
Proceed with the primary/secondary antibody protocol appropriate for each target (not detailed in the source).
Mount slides with Fluoromount‑G containing DAPI, cover with a coverslip, and store at 4 °C protected from light.
Avoid air bubbles under the coverslip and seal edges with nail polish or a suitable sealing agent.

steps.title: Confocal imaging of sections
steps.instruction: Acquire high‑resolution confocal images of stained tumor‑nerve sections using appropriate laser and detector settings.

substeps.instruction: Remove slides from 4 °C storage and equilibrate to room temperature.
Clean slide surfaces with a lint‑free, non‑abrasive cloth to remove debris.
Set microscope (e.g., Leica Stellaris 8 STED) parameters:
• DAPI – 360 nm excitation, laser 80 % power, 10 % Smart Power; Hybrid Detector 2, 400–470 nm filter, Smart Gain 2.5–50 %.
• eGFP – 488 nm excitation, laser 80 % power, 10 % Smart Power; Hybrid Detector 1, 500–570 nm filter, Smart Gain 2.5–50 %.
• Nav1.8‑tdTomato – 554 nm excitation, laser 80 % power, 10 % Smart Power; Hybrid Detector 1, 580–690 nm filter, Smart Gain 2.5–50 %.
Select objective: 10×/0.4 dry (low mag) or 20×/0.75 dry (high mag).
Use the tile acquisition tool to cover the entire tumor‑nerve region.
Perform Z‑stack acquisition with 2 µm step size to generate 3‑D datasets.
